questions.question: After allowing a discount of 64%, the value of a water cooler is ₹6,480. If no discount is allowed, then the shopkeeper gains 20%. Find the cost price (in ₹) of the water cooler

questions.question: If 3 is a common root of quadratic equations x² − 8x + P = 0 and x² + 4x + Q = 0, then find the value of P + Q.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Substitute the **common root** x = 3 into both equations directly.

First equation: 3² − 8(3) + P = 0 ⇒ 9 − 24 + P = 0 ⇒ **P = 15**.

Second equation: 3² + 4(3) + Q = 0 ⇒ 9 + 12 + Q = 0 ⇒ **Q = −21**.

Sum of constants: P + Q = 15 + (−21) = −6.

**∴ The correct answer is -6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: **x² − 8x + P = 0**

Equation 2: **x² + 4x + Q = 0**

Common Root: **x = 3**

**Formula Used:**

If a value α is a **root** of a quadratic equation f(x) = 0, then **f(α) = 0**.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Substituting x = 3 in the first equation:

⇒ (3)² − 8(3) + P = 0

⇒ 9 − 24 + P = 0

⇒ −15 + P = 0 ⇒ **P = 15**

⇒ Substituting x = 3 in the second equation:

⇒ (3)² + 4(3) + Q = 0

⇒ 9 + 12 + Q = 0

⇒ 21 + Q = 0 ⇒ **Q = −21**

⇒ To find the value of P + Q:

⇒ P + Q = 15 + (−21)

⇒ P + Q = −6

**∴ The correct answer is -6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Roots of Quadratic Equation

A root is a value that makes the polynomial equal to zero. For ax² + bx + c = 0, if α is a root, then aα² + bα + c = 0.

Sum and Product of Roots

For a quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the sum of roots is −b/a and the product of roots is c/a.

Condition for Common Root

If two equations a₁x² + b₁x + c₁ = 0 and a₂x² + b₂x + c₂ = 0 have a common root α, then α satisfies both, allowing us to eliminate α or solve for unknown coefficients.</p

questions.question: If the mode of a data set exceeds its mean by 17.7, then the mode exceeds the median by _____. (Use empirical formula.)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the direct relation derived from the **empirical formula**:

(**Mode** − **Median**) = 2/3 × (**Mode** − **Mean**)

Given: (**Mode** − **Mean**) = **17.7**

∴ (**Mode** − **Median**) = 2/3 × 17.7 = 2 × 5.9 = **11.8**

**∴ The correct answer is 11.8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Mode** − **Mean** = **17.7**

**Formula Used:** **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2624f18997784bb1414b2d7b4f6be8c98c52b6e478098d7881c7b4c4f1e488c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

⇒ **Mode** + 2 × **Mean** = 3 × **Median**

⇒ From given, **Mean** = **Mode** − 17.7

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × (**Mode** − 17.7)

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mode** + 35.4

⇒ 3 × **Mode** − 3 × **Median** = 35.4

⇒ 3 × (**Mode** − **Median**) = 35.4

⇒ **Mode** − **Median** = 35.4 ÷ 3

⇒ **Mode** − **Median** = **11.8**

**∴ The correct answer is 11.8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Empirical Formula

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship is **Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean**.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (**Mean = Median = Mode**).

Skewness Relation

The difference (**Mean** − **Mode**) is approximately three times the difference (**Mean** − **Median**).</p

questions.question: What sum of money (in ₹) will amount to ₹840 at 4% per annum simple interest in 3 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net **Simple Interest** percentage = Rate × Time = 4% × 3 = 12%

Total **Amount** percentage = 100% (Principal) + 12% (Interest) = 112%

Given, 112% → ₹840

Principal (100%) = (840 ÷ 112) × 100

Principal = 7.5 × 100 = ₹750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = ₹840

Rate (R) = 4% per annum

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d40281baef2856e5b779137acc328b90b6d6d7b6fc08598e05eaf7e4e5cf2de4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 840 = P + (P × 4 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 840 = P + 12P ÷ 100

⇒ 840 = (100P + 12P) ÷ 100

⇒ 840 = 112P ÷ 100

⇒ P = (840 × 100) ÷ 112

⇒ P = 7.5 × 100

⇒ P = ₹750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Principal Formula

When amount, rate, and time are given, Principal P = (100 × A) ÷ (100 + RT).

Simple Interest Property

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains constant every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Relationship between SI and Amount

Interest = Amount − Principal. In this case, SI = 840 − 750 = ₹90.

questions.question: Calculate the area of the triangle whose sides are 8 cm, 9 cm and 13 cm. (Rounded up to two decimal places)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify sides: **a = 8**, **b = 9**, **c = 13**.

Semi-perimeter **s = (8 + 9 + 13) ÷ 2 = 15 cm**.

Area = √[15 × (15 − 8) × (15 − 9) × (15 − 13)]

Area = √[15 × 7 × 6 × 2] = √1260 ≈ **35.50 cm²**.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.50 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sides of the **triangle**: **a = 8 cm**, **b = 9 cm**, **c = 13 cm**.

**Formula Used:**

**Heron's Formula**: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)]

Where **s** is the **semi-perimeter**: s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfc30231aa37dc43ac463ceaceb8d53f4cdc8b8e9fc991f0fae1826cc610645a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ s = (8 + 9 + 13) ÷ 2

⇒ s = 30 ÷ 2 = **15 cm**

⇒ Area = √[15 × (15 − 8) × (15 − 9) × (15 − 13)]

⇒ Area = √[15 × 7 × 6 × 2]

⇒ Area = √[1260]

⇒ Area ≈ **35.496 cm²**

⇒ Rounding to two decimal places, we get **35.50 cm²**.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.50 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used to find the area of any **triangle** when the lengths of all three sides are known. Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)].

Right-Angled Triangle Area

If the triangle is **right-angled**, the area can be simply calculated as 1/2 × **base** × **height**.

Equilateral Triangle Area

For a triangle with all equal sides **a**, Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × **a²**.</p

questions.question: The average price of three items of furniture is ₹15,255. If their prices are in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7, the price of the cheapest item (in ₹) is:

Total **ratio sum** = 3 + 5 + 7 = **15 units**.

Average ratio = 15 ÷ 3 = **5 units**.

Given **5 units** = **₹15,255** ⇒ 1 unit = **₹3,051**.

**Cheapest item** (3 units) = 3 × 3,051 = **₹9,153**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,153.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average price of **3 furniture items** = **₹15,255**

Ratio of their prices = **3 : 5 : 7**

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = **Average** × **Number of Observations**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the prices be **3x**, **5x**, and **7x**

⇒ 3x + 5x + 7x = 45,765

⇒ 15x = 45,765

⇒ x = 45,765 ÷ 15

⇒ x = **3,051**

⇒ Price of the cheapest item = 3x = 3 × 3,051

⇒ Cheapest item price = **₹9,153**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,153.**

**__Additional Information__**

Concept of Average

The average is the sum of all values divided by the total count. **Sum = Average × Count**.

questions.question: The Dutch East India Company's trade on the Coromandel Coast registered a significant increase over the 17th century due to:

the decline and collapse of the British influence in the region

• South-East Asia exhibited a rising demand for Indian textiles such as chintz, calicoes, and muslin due to their quality and intricate designs.
 
• The Dutch East India Company capitalized on this demand by expanding its trade network and establishing robust maritime routes linking India and South-East Asia.
 
• Indian textiles were used in barter trade by the Dutch to acquire spices, particularly from Indonesia, which further boosted commerce on the Coromandel Coast.
 
• The strategic presence of Dutch trading posts along the Coromandel Coast facilitated large-scale exports, cementing the region's importance in global trade during the 17th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Textiles as Trade Commodities:** Indian textiles were highly valued in South-East Asia, the Middle East, and Europe, often exchanged for spices, precious metals, and other goods.
 
• **Spice Trade Connection:** The Dutch used Indian textiles to acquire spices like nutmeg, cloves, and pepper from islands in South-East Asia, creating a mutually beneficial trade system.

questions.question: 6 : 42 :: 7.6 : x and 3 : 6 :: 6 : y. What is the ratio of x to y?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **Proportion** a : b :: c : d, the product of extremes equals the product of means (ad = bc).

Calculation for x: 6 × x = 42 × 7.6 ⇒ x = 7 × 7.6 = 53.2

Calculation for y: 3 × y = 6 × 6 ⇒ y = 12

Ratio x : y = 53.2 : 12 = 532 : 120 = 133 : 30

**∴ The correct answer is 133 : 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec0444ff50af536f6c6b21a1f99e692a2222d12bdccd39c411d8b5835611bb7d.png] 

**Given:** 6 : 42 :: 7.6 : x and 3 : 6 :: 6 : y

**Formula:** If a : b :: c : d, then a/b = c/d

⇒ 6/42 = 7.6/x

⇒ 1/7 = 7.6/x

⇒ x = 7.6 × 7 = 53.2

⇒ 3/6 = 6/y

⇒ 1/2 = 6/y

⇒ y = 6 × 2 = 12

⇒ x : y = 53.2 : 12

⇒ x : y = 532/10 : 12 = 532 : 120

⇒ x : y = 133 : 30

**∴ The correct answer is 133 : 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: c : d, **d** is called the fourth proportional, calculated as d = (b × c) / a.

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a : b :: b : c, then **c** is the third proportional, calculated as c = b² / a.</p

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 19 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 21 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill two-third of the tank?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling efficiency per minute = 1/19 − 1/21 = (21 − 19) / (19 × 21) = 2 / 399

Time to fill full tank = 399 / 2 minutes

Time to fill 2/3rd tank = (399 / 2) × (2 / 3) = 133 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 133 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time = 19 minutes, Emptying time = 21 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 **Pipe Type** **Time (min)** **Total Capacity (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 **Filling Pipe** 19 399 +21 
 **Emptying Pipe** 21 −19 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency of both pipes = 21 − 19 = 2 units/min

⇒ Required work = 2/3 of Total Capacity = (2/3) × 399 = 266 units

⇒ Required time = Required work ÷ Net efficiency

⇒ Required time = 266 ÷ 2 = 133 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 133 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Net Rate of Flow

When one pipe fills (rate x) and another empties (rate y), the combined rate is (1/x − 1/y) per unit time.

Pipes and Cisterns Logic

Inlet pipes contribute positive work (+) while Outlet pipes contribute negative work (−) towards filling the tank.

Partial Filling

Time taken to fill 'k' fraction of a tank = (k × Total Capacity) ÷ Net Efficiency.</p

questions.question: Who among the following spearheaded an active non-cooperation movement famously known as the ‘Barasat Rebellion’ against the British indigo planters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Titu Mir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Titu Mir** was a Bengali freedom fighter who led the 'Barasat Rebellion' against oppressive British indigo planters in Bengal.
 
• Born as Syed Mir Nisar Ali in 1782, Titu Mir used Islamic principles to unite farmers and weavers against exploitation.
 
• The rebellion occurred in 1831, where Titu Mir and his followers built a stronghold, the **bamboo fort** (Banser Kella), to resist British forces.
 
• He opposed the exploitative practices of indigo cultivation, high taxes, and the zamindari system enforced by British-backed landlords.
 
• Titu Mir was martyred in the struggle, but his movement is remembered as one of the early peasant revolts against British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigo Rebellion (1859-60):** Another significant peasant uprising in Bengal against the British indigo planters, where farmers refused to grow indigo due to exploitation.
 
• **Zamindari System:** Introduced by the British under the Permanent Settlement Act of 1793, this system empowered zamindars to collect taxes, often leading to severe exploitation of peasants.
 
• **Peasant Movements in India:** Titu Mir’s rebellion was one of the earliest organized uprisings, followed by others like the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56) and the Tebhaga Movement (1946-47).
 
• **Bamboo Fort:** Titu Mir’s fort was an innovative structure made of bamboo, symbolizing indigenous resistance against modern weaponry of the British.

questions.question: Which unique property of Plasmodium makes malaria a cyclical disease with periodic fever?

options.text: RBC rupture and toxin release every few days

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RBC rupture and toxin release every few days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The periodic fever in malaria is caused by the synchronous rupture of infected red blood cells (RBCs) and the release of toxins, primarily **hemozoin pigment and other inflammatory mediators**, into the bloodstream.
 
• Plasmodium parasites undergo a complex life cycle, including asexual reproduction within RBCs, leading to their destruction every 48-72 hours depending on the species.
 
• The cyclical nature of fever corresponds to the completion of the parasite's schizogony stage within RBCs, which is synchronized across a population of parasites.
 
• Species-specific periodicity: Plasmodium vivax and Plasmodium ovale cause fever every 48 hours, while Plasmodium malariae causes it every 72 hours, and Plasmodium falciparum often exhibits irregular fever patterns.
 
• The toxins and metabolites released during RBC rupture trigger immune responses, including the release of cytokines like **tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α)**, leading to fever and other systemic symptoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plasmodium Life Cycle:**

 
 
• The life cycle involves two hosts: humans and female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• In humans, Plasmodium first infects liver cells (exo-erythrocytic stage) and then moves to RBCs (erythrocytic stage).
 
 
 
• **Hemozoin:**
 
 
• A toxic byproduct of hemoglobin metabolism by Plasmodium parasites.
 
• Hemozoin accumulation is a key factor in triggering immune responses and systemic inflammation.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Fever Mechanism:**
 
 
• Caused by synchronized schizont rupture and immune system activation.
 
• Cytokines like TNF-α and interleukin-1 (IL-1) are released, leading to fever.
 
 
 
• **Plasmodium Species:**
 
 
• Four major human-infecting species: P. vivax, P. ovale, P. malariae, and P. falciparum.
 
• P. falciparum is the most dangerous, often causing severe and complicated malaria.
 
 
 
• **Malaria Transmission:**
 
 
• Spread via bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
 
• Control measures include insecticide-treated bed nets and antimalarial drugs.

questions.question: In a 2100 m circular race, Amit finishes one round in 42 seconds and Sumit finishes one round in 75 seconds. How many different meeting points are there on the circumference if they are running in the opposite directions?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **time taken** by Amit and Sumit to complete one round = 42 : 75 = 14 : 25.

Since **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time**, Ratio of **speeds** (u : v) = 25 : 14.

For **opposite directions**, Number of **distinct meeting points** = u + v.

Number of meeting points = 25 + 14 = 39.

**∴ The correct answer is 39 points.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f727ed306389e418b547665a2b1c7d04282eb26753ce525182e638f4d99805af.png] 

**Given:** Track Length = 2100 m, TAₘᵢₜ = 42 s, TSᵤₘᵢₜ = 75 s.

**Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Distinct points (opposite) = Ratio of speeds (a + b) where a/b is in simplest form.

⇒ Speed of Amit (SA) = 2100 ÷ 42 = 50 m/s

⇒ Speed of Sumit (SS) = 2100 ÷ 75 = 28 m/s

⇒ Ratio of Speeds SA : SS = 50 : 28

⇒ Simplest Ratio = 25 : 14

⇒ Number of distinct meeting points = 25 + 14 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39 points.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Points in Same Direction

If two people run in the **same direction** with speeds in the simplest ratio a : b (a > b), the number of distinct meeting points is (a − b).

Time of First Meeting

The time taken for the **first meeting anywhere** on the track is Track Length ÷ Relative Speed.

Time of Meeting at Starting Point

The time when they meet for the first time at the **starting point** is the LCM of the time taken by each to complete one full round.</p

questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution does the High Court exercise its original jurisdiction by issuing writs?

__
 
• Article 226 of the Indian Constitution empowers High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and other legal rights.
 
• The writ jurisdiction includes issuing writs like habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, and quo warranto.
 
• Unlike Article 32 (Supreme Court), Article 226 covers not only fundamental rights but also other rights established by law.
 
• The High Court's writ jurisdiction extends to persons, authorities, and governments within its territorial limits.
 
• Article 226 serves as a vital mechanism for judicial review and upholding the rule of law in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Prohibition:** Prevents lower courts from exceeding their jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari:** Transfers cases to higher courts for review.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** Challenges the legality of a person's public office holding.
 
 
 
• **Article 32 vs Article 226:**
 
 
• Article 32 is limited to enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
• Article 226 includes fundamental rights and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Territorial Jurisdiction:** High Courts can exercise writ jurisdiction over entities within their geographical boundaries.
 
• **Judicial Review:** Article 226 plays a crucial role in ensuring the accountability of public authorities and safeguarding individual rights.
 
• **Importance:** Article 226 is considered broader in scope than Article 32 and is essential for maintaining constitutional governance.

questions.question: Which of the options below is equivalent to 216x³ + 343y³ + 756x²y + 882xy²
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **cubic terms** in the expression: 216x³ and 343y³.

Since **√³(216x³) = 6x** and **√³(343y³) = 7y**, the base terms are 6x and 7y.

The expression follows the expansion of **(a + b)³** where all terms are positive.

Checking middle terms: 3(6x)²(7y) = 756x²y and 3(6x)(7y)² = 882xy².

**∴ The correct answer is (6x + 7y)³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 216x³ + 343y³ + 756x²y + 882xy²

**Formula Used:** (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3a²b + 3ab²

⇒ Rewrite 216x³ as (6x)³

⇒ Rewrite 343y³ as (7y)³

⇒ Express 756x²y as 3 × (6x)² × (7y) = 3 × 36x² × 7y = 756x²y

⇒ Express 882xy² as 3 × (6x) × (7y)² = 3 × 6x × 49y² = 882xy²

⇒ The given expression is now: (6x)³ + (7y)³ + 3(6x)²(7y) + 3(6x)(7y)²

⇒ This is the standard expansion of (6x + 7y)³.

**∴ The correct answer is (6x + 7y)³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cube of Difference Identity

(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3a²b + 3ab², which involves alternating signs.

Sum of Two Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). This is a factorisation identity, not a perfect cube expansion.

Difference of Two Cubes

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Perfect Cube Recognition

Common cubes include 6³ = 216, 7³ = 343, 8³ = 512, and 9³ = 729.</p

questions.question: Which of the following options best explains the temporary cessation of rainfall during the southwest monsoon over parts of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Break in monsoon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "Break in monsoon" refers to a temporary pause or reduction in rainfall during the southwest monsoon season in India.
 
• It occurs due to a weakening or shift of the monsoon trough away from its normal position over the Indian subcontinent.
 
• During this period, rainfall decreases significantly over central and northern parts of India, while the southern regions may still experience scattered showers.
 
• The break in monsoon is often associated with atmospheric subsidence or stable air conditions that inhibit cloud formation and precipitation.
 
• These breaks are a characteristic feature of the southwest monsoon and may last for several days before the rainfall resumes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Southwest Monsoon:**

 
 
• The southwest monsoon typically lasts from June to September and is the primary rainy season in India.
 
• It is driven by the cross-equatorial moisture-laden winds originating from the Indian Ocean.
 
• Monsoon activity is influenced by factors such as the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) and the Himalayan geography.
 
 
 
• **Monsoon Trough:**
 
 
• The monsoon trough is an elongated low-pressure area extending from the northwest to the southeast across the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Its position and intensity significantly affect monsoon rainfall patterns.
 
 
 
• **Subtropical Jet Stream:**
 
 
• During the monsoon season, the subtropical jet stream shifts northward, allowing the monsoon winds to penetrate the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Any interference or unusual positioning of this jet stream can impact monsoon activity.
 
 
 
• **Cross-Equatorial Surge:**
 
 
• A phenomenon involving strong winds from the southern hemisphere crossing the equator to feed the monsoon system in India.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the onset and progression of the southwest monsoon.
 
 
 
• **Break Periods:**
 
 
• Break periods in the monsoon are not uncommon and are marked by reduced rainfall over large parts of the country.
 
• These pauses are usually short-lived and do not indicate the end of the monsoon season.

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 72 minutes and 76 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 54 minutes?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Pipe A** works for the entire **54 minutes**.

Work done by **Pipe A** in 54 min = 54 ÷ 72 = 3/4 of the total capacity.

Remaining work to be done by **Pipe B** = 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.

Time for which **Pipe B** was open = (1/4) × 76 = 19 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **Pipe A** = 72 min; Time taken by **Pipe B** = 76 min; Total time = 54 min.

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **Pipe A** 72 min 1368 units 19
 **Pipe B** 76 min 18
**Formula:** Total Work = (Efficiency × Time)

⇒ Let **Pipe B** be closed after **'x' minutes**.

⇒ Total work = (Efficiency of A × 54) + (Efficiency of B × x)

⇒ 1368 = (19 × 54) + (18 × x)

⇒ 1368 = 1026 + 18x

⇒ 18x = 1368 − 1026

⇒ 18x = 342

⇒ x = 342 ÷ 18 = 19 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 19 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

The efficiency of a pipe is inversely proportional to the time taken to fill or empty a cistern. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time.

Combined Work Formula

If two pipes A and B can fill a tank in x and y hours respectively, their 1 hour's work is (1/x + 1/y). Combined time = (xy)/(x + y).

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

Inlet pipe efficiency is positive (+), while outlet (leakage) pipe efficiency is negative (−). Net work = Σ Efficiency × Time.</p

questions.question:

 II. A discount of 7% followed by a discount of 6%

 III. Successive discounts of 45% and 29%

 IV. A discount of 20% followed by a discount of 38%

 Which scheme will fetch the maximum selling price?

To obtain the **Maximum Selling Price**, the **Total Discount** percentage must be the **minimum**.

Successive discount formula: **a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)**.

Scheme I: 27 + 27 − 7.29 = 46.71% | Scheme II: 7 + 6 − 0.42 = 12.58%.

Scheme III: 45 + 29 − 13.05 = 60.95% | Scheme IV: 20 + 38 − 7.6 = 50.4%.

Comparing all, **Scheme II** has the lowest discount, resulting in the highest SP.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Four different **successive discount** schemes.
Formulas: Net Discount % = a + b − (a × b ÷ 100) | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4224eb495d0a1983a389be4f1f0047a25bc0f6e3c1c788d2d31f540742925fa.png] 
⇒ Calculate effective discount for Scheme I: 27 + 27 − (27 × 27 ÷ 100) = 54 − 7.29 = **46.71%**.
⇒ Calculate effective discount for Scheme II: 7 + 6 − (7 × 6 ÷ 100) = 13 − 0.42 = **12.58%**.
⇒ Calculate effective discount for Scheme III: 45 + 29 − (45 × 29 ÷ 100) = 74 − 13.05 = **60.95%**.
⇒ Calculate effective discount for Scheme IV: 20 + 38 − (20 × 38 ÷ 100) = 58 − 7.6 = **50.4%**.
⇒ Comparing all schemes, 12.58% (Scheme II) is the **minimum discount**.
⇒ Since Selling Price = MP − Discount, the minimum discount yields the **maximum Selling Price**.

**∴ The correct answer is II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

The **Marked Price (MP)** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the MP unless stated otherwise. **Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount**.

Successive Discounts

When multiple discounts are applied one after another, the net discount is less than the simple sum of individual percentages because subsequent discounts are applied to the already reduced price.</p

questions.question: The sum of 6 numbers is 288. Find their average.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **average** is the **sum** divided by the **count**.

Direct calculation: 288 ÷ 6 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **sum** of 6 numbers = 288

Total **quantity** (n) = 6

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/71fe99c224a21ca69c7f4db2892f21ff28c308b7eec7e7db3ed21cf326125077.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average = 288 ÷ 6

⇒ Average = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, the average is simply (First term + Last term) ÷ 2.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Effect of Operations on Average

If every number in a set is increased, decreased, multiplied, or divided by a constant **k**, the **average** also changes by that same constant **k**.</p

questions.question: Which of the following statements about RAM and ROM with reference to computer memory is correct?

options.text: RAM cannot be written to, only read from.
RAM temporarily stores data for active programs, while ROM permanently stores firmware.
RAM is non-volatile, while ROM is volatile.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM temporarily stores data for active programs, while ROM permanently stores firmware**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory)** is a volatile memory that temporarily stores data for active programs and processes.
 
• **ROM (Read-Only Memory)** is a non-volatile memory that permanently stores firmware or essential instructions required for booting up the system.
 
• RAM is faster than ROM because it is designed to handle data at high speeds for real-time operations.
 
• Unlike RAM, which loses its data when the system is powered off, ROM retains its data even without power.
 
• ROM is primarily used for storage of critical instructions (e.g., BIOS), while RAM is used for dynamic data processing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Volatile vs Non-Volatile Memory:** Volatile memory (e.g., RAM) requires constant power to retain data, while non-volatile memory (e.g., ROM) retains data even when power is lost.
 
• **Firmware:** Firmware refers to the permanent software programmed into ROM that provides low-level control for a device's hardware.
 
• **RAM Types:** Common types of RAM include DRAM (Dynamic RAM) and SRAM (Static RAM). DRAM is slower and cheaper, while SRAM is faster and more expensive.
 
• **ROM Variants:** ROM comes in various types such as PROM (Programmable ROM), EPROM (Erasable Programmable ROM), and EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM).
 
• **Importance of RAM:** Higher RAM capacity allows for better multitasking and faster processing of applications, making it a critical component for system performance.

questions.question: The sum of the age of A and 4 times the age of B is 37 years. When 7 times the age of A is added to 6 times the age of B, the result is 61 years. The sum of the ages (in years) of A and B is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the ages of **A** and **B** be **A** and **B** years respectively.

Given: **A + 4B = 37** and **7A + 6B = 61**.

Multiply the first equation by 7: **7A + 28B = 259**.

Subtract the second equation from this: **(7A + 28B) − (7A + 6B) = 259 − 61** ⇒ **22B = 198** ⇒ **B = 9**.

Substitute **B = 9** in the first equation: **A + 4(9) = 37** ⇒ **A = 37 − 36 = 1**.

Sum of ages = **1 + 9 = 10**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67251d7e146ccfaa5c77d7febec0342bdbf3d6fb890f00ca5db818cc1ad819df.png] 

**Given:**

Equation 1: **A + 4B = 37**

Equation 2: **7A + 6B = 61**

**Calculations:**

⇒ From (1): **A = 37 − 4B**

⇒ Substitute in (2): **7(37 − 4B) + 6B = 61**

⇒ **259 − 28B + 6B = 61**

⇒ **259 − 22B = 61**

⇒ **22B = 198**

⇒ **B = 9**

⇒ Now, **A = 37 − 4(9) = 37 − 36 = 1**

⇒ Sum of ages = **A + B = 1 + 9 = 10**

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Two Variables

Problems involving two unknowns require a system of two independent equations to find unique values for each variable.

Elimination Method

Multiply equations by suitable constants so that the coefficients of one variable become equal, allowing its removal by subtraction or addition.

Ages Concept

If the current age is **x**, then age **n** years ago was **x − n** and age **n** years hence will be **x + n**.</p

questions.question: Which of the following acts of the East India Company mandated that selection for civil employees in British Indian territory would be based on the competitive examinations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Charter Act 1853**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1853** was the last Charter Act passed by the British Parliament concerning the East India Company.
 
• This Act introduced an open and competitive system of recruitment for civil services, marking a significant departure from the patronage system.
 
• The Act mandated that civil service positions in the British Indian administration would be filled through a competitive examination process.
 
• The competitive examinations were to be conducted in England, and the system was open to all British citizens, including Indians, although Indians faced significant barriers initially.
 
• The Act reflected growing demands for administrative reforms and efficiency in the governance of British India.

• **Charter Act of 1793:** This Act renewed the East India Company's charter for 20 years but did not introduce any significant administrative reforms.
 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784:** It established a dual system of governance, creating the Board of Control to supervise the East India Company’s civil, military, and revenue affairs.
 
• **Charter Act of 1813:** This Act ended the East India Company’s trade monopoly in India, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• **Impact of the Charter Act of 1853:** It was the first step toward introducing a merit-based system in Indian civil services, which was later formalized under the Indian Civil Service Act of 1861.
 
• **Significance of Competitive Exams:** The provision for competitive examinations laid the foundation for modern civil services in India and reflected the influence of liberal ideas of equality and meritocracy.

questions.question: A person who spends 75% of his monthly income is able to save ₹5,538 per month. His monthly expenses (in ₹) are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Savings %** = 100% − 75% = 25%

According to the question, 25% = ₹5,538

**Monthly Expenses** (75%) = 3 × 25%

**Monthly Expenses** = 3 × 5,538 = ₹16,614

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,614.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **Total Income** be ₹x

⇒ Savings % = 100% − 75% = 25%

⇒ 25% of x = 5,538

⇒ (25/100) × x = 5,538

⇒ x/4 = 5,538

⇒ x = 5,538 × 4 = 22,152

⇒ Monthly Expenses = 75% of 22,152

⇒ Monthly Expenses = (3/4) × 22,152

⇒ Monthly Expenses = 3 × 5,538 = 16,614

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16,614.**

When income is taken as 100, any change in expenditure or savings directly translates to a change in the total base value.

Ratio Method

The ratio of Expenses to Savings is 75:25 or 3:1. If 1 unit represents ₹5,538, then 3 units represent the expenses.

Income Formula

Income = Savings ÷ (1 − Expense Rate). This helps in finding total income directly from savings and expense percentage.

questions.question: Which major discovery helps to design drugs in the treatment of hyperacidity?

options.text: The role of enzymes in digestion
The use of antibiotics to neutralize stomach acid
Hydrochloric acid present in the stomach
Histamine stimulates acid secretion in the stomach

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Histamine stimulates acid secretion in the stomach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Histamine plays a crucial role** in stimulating the secretion of gastric acid in the stomach by binding to H2 receptors on the parietal cells.
 
• This discovery has been instrumental in the development of **H2 receptor antagonists** such as ranitidine and famotidine, which are widely used to treat hyperacidity and related disorders.
 
• Histamine-mediated acid secretion is an important target in the treatment of conditions like **gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic ulcers, and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome**.
 
• The regulation of histamine pathways has also led to advancements in **proton pump inhibitors (PPIs)**, which further reduce gastric acid production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Histamine:** A chemical messenger released by certain cells in the body, including mast cells, that plays a key role in immune responses and gastric acid secretion.
 
• **H2 Receptor Antagonists:** Drugs like ranitidine and cimetidine that block histamine H2 receptors, reducing stomach acid production and relieving symptoms of hyperacidity.
 
• **Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs):** Medications such as omeprazole and esomeprazole that inhibit the final step in acid secretion, providing long-lasting relief for acid-related conditions.
 
• **Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD):** A chronic condition where stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing irritation and requiring acid-suppressing treatments.
 
• **Parietal Cells:** Specialized cells in the stomach lining that produce hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor, essential for digestion and vitamin B12 absorption.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India states about a directive to states for the settlement of international disputes by arbitration?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51 of the Indian Constitution falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) and promotes international peace and security.
 
• Clause (d) of Article 51 specifically encouraging the settlement of international disputes by arbitration.
 
• It emphasizes the peaceful resolution of international disputes through arbitration.
 
• This article reflects India’s commitment to maintaining amicable and cooperative international relations.
 
• It aligns with the principles of the United Nations Charter, promoting global harmony and dispute resolution.

• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• The DPSPs are guidelines for the State to establish a just and equitable society, enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution.
 
• They are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by courts but hold moral and political significance.
 
 
 
• **Arbitration in International Law:**
 
 
• Arbitration is a method of resolving disputes outside courts, where a neutral third party (arbitrator) gives a binding decision.
 
• It is commonly used in international disputes to avoid prolonged litigation and maintain diplomatic relationships.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Charter:**
 
 
• The UN Charter, established in 1945, is the foundational treaty of the United Nations and promotes peace, security, and cooperation among nations.
 
• India, being a founding member of the UN, aligns its constitutional provisions like Article 51 with the principles of the Charter.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is NOT a major river of the Great Plateau (Peninsular Plateau) of India?

• The Yamuna originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Himalayas and flows through states like Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi.
 
• Rivers of the Peninsular Plateau, such as the Narmada, Godavari, and Krishna, have distinct east-west drainage patterns shaped by the plateau's topography.
 
• The Yamuna is part of the Ganga river basin, which is geographically separate from the rivers of the Peninsular Plateau.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau Rivers:**

 
 
• The Narmada and Tapti are west-flowing rivers, draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The Krishna, Godavari, and Kaveri are east-flowing rivers, draining into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan vs. Peninsular Rivers:**
 
 
• Himalayan rivers like the Yamuna are perennial and fed by glaciers and rainfall.
 
• Peninsular rivers are mostly rain-fed and have seasonal flow patterns.

• The Yamuna lies to the north of the Vindhya range, outside the Peninsular Plateau region.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by both 43 and 32?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check divisibility by **32** first: A number is divisible by **32** if its last 5 digits are divisible by **32**, or use **8 × 4**.

Option (1) 136224: Last three digits 224 ÷ 8 = 28 (Divisible by 8) and 224 ÷ 32 = 7 (Last 5 digits 36224 ÷ 32 = 1132).

Check divisibility by **43**: 136224 ÷ 43 = 3168.

Since 136224 is divisible by both, it is the answer.

**∴ The correct answer is 136224.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Divisors are **43** and **32**.

**Formula Used:** If a number is divisible by two **co-prime numbers**, it is divisible by their **product**.

⇒ Required number must be a multiple of **LCM(43, 32)**.

⇒ Since 43 is a **prime number**, LCM = 43 × 32.

⇒ LCM = 1376.

⇒ Now, check which option is divisible by **1376**:

⇒ 136224 ÷ 1376 = 99.

⇒ 135131 ÷ 1376 ≈ 98.20.

⇒ 137005 ÷ 1376 ≈ 99.56.

⇒ 137868 ÷ 1376 ≈ 100.19.

**∴ The correct answer is 136224.**

Divisibility Rule of 32

A number is divisible by **32** (2⁵) if the number formed by its last **5 digits** is divisible by 32.

Divisibility Rule of Prime Numbers

For a prime number **p** like 43, use the **oscillator method**. For 43, the osculator is 13 (43 → 4×10 + 3, multiplier = 13). Multiply the last digit by 13 and add to the remaining part.

LCM of Co-prime Numbers

The **Least Common Multiple** of two co-prime numbers **a** and **b** is always their product **a × b**.</p

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio 5 : 1 : 7, and their LCM is 7595. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **HCF** be **x**.

Numbers are **5x, 1x, and 7x**.

Since 5, 1, and 7 are **coprime**, their **LCM** = 5 × 1 × 7 × x = 35x.

35x = 7595 ⇒ x = 7595 ÷ 35 = 217.

**∴ The correct answer is 217.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of numbers = **5 : 1 : 7**, **LCM** = **7595**.

**Formula:** LCM of numbers = **HCF × product of ratios** (if ratios are coprime).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/402a34c2067aca19636d1a8d6d0a7ed73226cf96a151f2d56b1d18cbf227179c.png] 

⇒ Let the numbers be **5k, k, and 7k**, where **k** is the **HCF**.

⇒ LCM(5k, k, 7k) = k × LCM(5, 1, 7)

⇒ Since 5 and 7 are **prime numbers**, LCM(5, 1, 7) = 5 × 7 = 35.

⇒ 35k = 7595

⇒ k = 7595 ÷ 35

⇒ k = 217

**∴ The correct answer is 217.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Relation

For two numbers A and B: **Product of Numbers = HCF × LCM**.

Coprime Numbers

If numbers are **coprime**, their **HCF is always 1** and their **LCM is the product** of the numbers.

Fractional LCM/HCF

LCM of Fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators. HCF of Fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.</p

questions.question: Walking at 4/5 of his normal speed, Vishal is 25 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Speed ratio** is given as 4 : 5 (New : Normal).

Since **distance** is constant, the **time ratio** is the inverse of the speed ratio, i.e., 5 : 4.

Difference in time units = 5 − 4 = 1 unit.

Given, 1 unit = 25 minutes.

Usual time (4 units) = 4 × 25 = 100 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb5e3384fe6a00f1a251d495ba1e99b6f188f691fa87bfbe5b1af03429f6aa78.png] 

**Given:**

New Speed = 4/5 of Normal Speed

Time delay = 25 minutes

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time | If Distance is constant, Speed₁ × Time₁ = Speed₂ × Time₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let usual speed be **S** and usual time be **T**.

⇒ New speed = (4/5)S and New time = T + 25

⇒ S × T = (4/5)S × (T + 25)

⇒ T = (4/5)(T + 25)

⇒ 5T = 4T + 100

⇒ T = 100 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inversely Proportional Relation

When **Distance** is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time** (S ∝ 1/T). If speed becomes a/b of its original, time becomes b/a of its original.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. For opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed Formula

When equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p

x = 34
